key_insight: Connected speech in psychosis appears less efficiently compressed, with grammar-related signals predicting weaker information compression.
clinical_relevance: This suggests language analysis with LLM-based metrics may help quantify speech abnormalities in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, including early psychosis.
method: Analyzed connected speech from 144 Turkish speakers using word-frequency surprisal and contextual LLM surprisal.
Estimated compressibility via intrinsic dimensionality of speech representations.
Tested how syntactic complexity and compressibility relate to surprisal difference across patient and control groups.
evidence_signal: In 106 patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders versus 38 controls, surprisal difference was lower in all clinical groups, while compressibility was reduced in chronic schizophrenia and first-episode psychosis.
watch_item: Findings are group-level and language-specific, so clinical use would require careful validation across languages, settings, and recording conditions.
paper_title: Psychosis involves a deficit of information compression in connected speech
